name: filetree
description: An IDE-style file tree for Claude Code that shows what Claude is doing and where in files

activity.title: Show activity
activity.description: Which of Claude's file activity shimmers in the tree: files read with the Read tool or Bash readers (rg, grep, find, cat), writes and git actions. In the desktop app they take the skin's colours (writes in the accent, git in green); in the terminal reads are purple, writes orange and git green

glyphs.title: Icons
glyphs.description: Icon set: auto uses Nerd Font icons when one is installed here, and no type glyphs in the desktop app; plain uses Unicode only; nerd always uses Nerd Font

follow.title: Follow Claude
follow.description: on: the tree scrolls to what Claude reads, writes or commits. off: the view stays where you put it and only your own scrolling moves it; highlights still show.

start.title: Open at start
start.description: on: the pane opens when a session starts. off: it stays closed until you open it from /mods.

column.title: Right column
column.description: What the right column shows by default: date (last modified), age (time since last modified, short: now, 12m, 3h, 5d, then Oct 9 past a week and the year past a year) or size (files in bytes, folders as disk usage computed in the background). The Sizes header button toggles between size and the date or age.

hints.title: No-repo hint
hints.description: on: outside a git repo, a line under the header says git status starts after git init. off: the line is hidden and the tree gets the row.

open.title: Open with
open.description: What a double-click or Enter does with a file. Empty: the default app. preview: show it in the pane (left goes back). Anything else is a command run instead: {path} is the file and {dir} its folder; without {path} the path goes last. Words split on spaces, quotes keep a word whole, and no shell runs it. It should start the viewer and return; on Linux it runs detached.
